insight.title: Why Faster Tools Create More Busywork
insight.subtitle: How saving time leads to a more crowded schedule

sections.text: Most businesses invest heavily to shave seconds off a process. Yet, when tasks get faster, your schedule rarely gets lighter. You don’t gain time; you simply lower your standards for what is important.
We adjust our behavior based on the perceived cost of an action. When sending a message becomes instant, we send ten shallow notes instead of one thoughtful response that actually moves the needle.
Strategy suffers when resources feel abundant. When time is cheap, we stop being selective. We trade high-intensity focus for a series of low-stakes tasks that keep us busy while the big goals stall.
Try this today: When you finish a task early today, pause for ten seconds before starting anything else.
Speed is only a competitive advantage if you have the discipline to stay still.
